name: Dusty hunter green
lede: Dusty hunter green is a muted, dark green, ColorHub's English name for the Japanese traditional color Tokusa-iro, "horsetail color," after the horsetail plant.

sections.title: The horsetail plant
sections.body:
Tokusa-iro (木賊色) is named in the Wikipedia list of Japan's traditional colors for *tokusa*, the horsetail (*Equisetum*), whose stiff dark-green stems the color recalls [1]. Horsetail stems were also used in Japan as a natural abrasive for polishing wood and metal, though the sources consulted do not say whether that use shaped the name [1].

The nearest named colors on file are [[hunter-green]] and [[empire-green]], at Both sit within the library's Greens family, alongside the core color [[green|Green]] [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this color in 173 of 23,781 paintings, under one percent, as photographed [2]. The earliest match is a 1400 Rijksmuseum portrait group, *De heren van Montfoort*, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2]. The rate is highest in a sample of 523 paintings from the 1910s, nearly five times the archive average for that decade [2]. It is disproportionately present among Post-Impressionist painters sampled in our archive, including Henri Rousseau, Paul Gauguin, Camille Pissarro and Paul Cézanne [2]. The United States, Sweden, Norway, Switzerland and France all show it above their average rate [2]. These are computed color matches to photographed, varnished paintings, not pigment identifications [2].
